correctness.rationale: Sorting both s-component probability vectors yields a signed step function h(t)=Σ(1_{p_i>t}−1_{r_i>t}) with at most s−1 sign changes: supports from opposite-signed intervals at increasing indices are disjoint and ordered. The Mellin transform M(z)=∫t^z h(t)dt is a real exponential-polynomial integral with at most s−1 real zeros counted with multiplicity by the confluent Chebyshev/zero-variation lemma, proved via Rolle and sign interpolation. F(q)=Σp_i^q−Σr_i^q=q M(q−1); normalization M(0)=0 consumes one zero, and at q=1 the Shannon tie requires M′(0)=0. Therefore there are ≤s−2 finite q>0 ties for unequal multisets. Independent exact integer power sums for the displayed P and Q gave F(2),F(3),F(4) signs +,−,+ with differences 2362, −517776, 16323602434, hence exactly two simple crossings, in (2,3) and (3,4). No assertion of s−2 attainability for every s≥5.

originality.rationale: General Rényi/Hill diversity comparison and crossing examples predate this record. Leinster–Cobbold 2012 explicitly exhibit two profile crossings but do not in the inspected corresponding section determine minimal positive species count. value.rationale: Hill/Rényi profiles are standard diversity-orderings in ecology; an upper bound on ranking reversals in terms of richness and an exact smallest double-reversal example clarify a natural model-selection ambiguity. The s=4 threshold is supported by an all-s theorem, not merely a numerical curiosity.
